title: Ada and the Alibi
premise: Retired detective Rafael Okonkwo has spent seven years hiding in a failing bookshop, haunted by the unsolved disappearance of Ada Voss, a case the town swore was closed when her husband confessed by suicide note. When a letter arrives postmarked the day after Ada's funeral—written in her handwriting, confessing she faked her death—Rafael is pulled back into the case everyone forbade reopening. As the trial of Ada's accused killer approaches, Rafael uncovers a conspiracy among the town's most respected citizens, including the person who taught them to trust their instincts. In the end, Rafael must choose between protecting the town's fragile peace and the truth, exposing Ada alive but complicit in a scheme to escape an abusive marriage, and accepting that belonging means being seen, even when it costs everything.
about_author: Isandro Hartwell is a former small-town court reporter who spent a decade transcribing the secrets of one fading coastal community before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about people who mistake silence for safety.

chapters.title: Postmark
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. In the failing bookshop, Rafael opens a letter postmarked the day after Ada Voss's funeral, written in her unmistakable hand. The emotional beat is dread disguised as routine—the past knocking politely.

chapters.title: The Case That Closed Itself
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, with flashback. Rafael recalls how the town celebrated when Ada's husband confessed by note and died, and how Rafael's superiors buried their doubts. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing like a bruise pressed on purpose.

chapters.title: Trial Date
chapters.summary: Rafael visits the courthouse and learns the man accused of Ada's murder—her brother-in-law—goes to trial in five weeks. The prosecutor warns Rafael off. Emotional beat: the clock starting, the first refusal.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Examining the confession letter's paper and phrasing, Rafael finds references to books Ada borrowed from the shop years ago. Emotional beat: hope flickering against professional skepticism—someone knows Rafael's inventory intimately.

chapters.title: The Widow's Sister
chapters.summary: Ada's sister, Nell, arrives at the bookshop, ostensibly to buy a novel, actually to ask what Rafael received in the mail. Rafael lies for the first time in the story. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to war with truth.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, reflective. A slow chapter tracing Rafael's retirement, the shop's debts, and the friendship with neighbor Dot, the retired coroner who signed Ada's death certificate. Emotional beat: what invisibility has cost.

chapters.title: Dot's Signature
chapters.summary: Rafael confronts Dot, who admits she identified the body but was pressured to expedite the paperwork. Emotional beat: betrayal—Rafael's oldest friend was part of the machinery of closure.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A second letter arrives, this one containing a bus ticket stub and a warning: stop asking, or the trial gets messier. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into stubbornness—Rafael can't close what they can't open.

chapters.title: Inland
chapters.summary: Rafael follows the ticket stub to an inland town, finding a woman who resembles Ada working in a garden center. She denies everything, but her hands shake. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt returning after seven dormant years.

chapters.title: What the Husband Knew
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, digging into the dead husband's affairs. His suicide note was typed, not handwritten, and his finances were drained the week before. Emotional beat: the confession was purchased, and someone with money did the buying.

chapters.title: The Mentor
chapters.summary: Rafael visits former chief Inspector Halloran, who taught them the trade, and finds Ada's photograph on his desk. Emotional beat: the floor giving way—Rafael's compass of trust points to the person who built it.

chapters.title: Nell's Confession
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell reveals she helped Ada disappear to escape the husband's abuse, and that Halloran facilitated it—then began blackmailing Ada for silence. Emotional beat: compassion colliding with fury; every ally has a ledger.

chapters.title: The Man on Trial
chapters.summary: Rafael interviews the accused brother-in-law in jail, who confesses he suspected the body wasn't Ada but said nothing because he hated his brother. Emotional beat: an innocent man choosing silence—loyalty's ugliest form.

chapters.title: Blackmail Ledger
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Following Halloran's money, Rafael finds payments routed through a shell charity—along with donations from half the town council. Emotional beat: the conspiracy is bigger than one bad cop; the whole town bought its peace.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Rafael's bookshop is broken into; the letters and notes are stolen, and a fire is started in the history section. Dot pulls Rafael from the smoke. Emotional beat: the cost of visibility made literal—Rafael can no longer pretend to be safe.

chapters.title: Ada, Actually
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The woman in the garden center is Ada herself. She explains the plan, her guilt over the brother-in-law's trial, and her offer: disappear forever, and Rafael gets their quiet life back. Emotional beat: temptation, offered gently.

chapters.title: The Deal Refused
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael tells Ada the truth can't be rationed—that the innocent man on trial is the price of her freedom, and Rafael won't pay it. Ada's choice hangs. Emotional beat: Rafael choosing truth over belonging, finally.

chapters.title: Halloran's House
chapters.summary: Rafael and Nell break into Halloran's home for the ledger originals, but Halloran is waiting. A tense standoff; he argues he saved Ada and the town both. Emotional beat: the climax of ideology—two detectives, one broken compass.

chapters.title: What Rafael Swore
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael records Halloran admitting the scheme, then turns the recording over—not to the prosecutor, but to Ada, giving her one day to come forward on her own terms. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth reconciled, briefly.

chapters.title: The Woman in Court
chapters.summary: Ada walks into the courtroom alive on the trial's second day. The town's reaction is volcanic; Halloran is arrested; the brother-in-law walks free. Emotional beat: catharsis and chaos—the truth arriving like weather.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Ada, facing charges for faking her death, asks Rafael to testify to the abuse that drove her. Rafael does, publicly, ending their own invisibility. Emotional beat: identity claimed at last, at cost.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, months later. The shop reopens with new shelves and a hand-painted sign; Ada, sentenced to community service, works there part-time. Rafael finally takes down the old case file. Emotional beat: belonging earned, quiet rebuilt on truth instead of silence.
